Expedia Group Interview Experience.
Compensation Range: 35+ LPA
Role: Data Engineer
Application Method: Referral

𝟭𝘀𝘁 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 – 𝗛𝗶𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗿 (𝗘𝗹𝗶𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱)

- Deep dive into project architecture
- Heavy focus on streaming systems – recurring theme at Expedia
- Advanced discussion on:
 Kafka: Backpressure, design challenges
- Database internals: Indexing, partitioning, connection pooling
- Strong emphasis on fundamentals and system-level thinking

𝟮𝗻𝗱 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 – 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 + 𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘀

- Extensive discussion on: Microservices: APIs, JWT, SAML authentication
- Spark Internals: Execution plan, memory, transformations/actions
- At least 25–30 technical questions asked
- Focus aligned with resume content (e.g., microservices, Spark)

𝟯𝗿𝗱 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 – 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 + 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴

- Started with programming (tricky array-based problem)
- Follow-up: Design a streaming system end-to-end
- Topics:
 Kafka, Spark Streaming
 Expectations to know Flink (optional)
 Real-time data design and processing focus

𝟰𝘁𝗵 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 – 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁 & 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗵𝗼𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁

- End-to-end data pipeline implementation
- SDLC process: From requirement to deployment
- Behavioral Questions (STAR format):
 Team conflict resolution
 Role models, ownership, communication

ai_analysis.summary: This post summarizes a four-round Expedia Group Data Engineer interview experience, with a stated compensation range of 35+ LPA and a referral application method. The first round covered project architecture, streaming systems, Kafka backpressure and design challenges, database indexing, partitioning, connection pooling, and system-level fundamentals. The second covered microservices, APIs, JWT, SAML, and Spark execution plans, memory, transformations, and actions; the post reports at least 25–30 technical questions aligned with the resume. The third began with a tricky array-based programming problem and continued with an end-to-end streaming-system design involving Kafka and Spark Streaming, with Flink listed as optional. The fourth covered an end-to-end data pipeline from requirements through deployment and STAR-format questions about conflict resolution, role models, ownership, and communication. The post does not provide technical answers, architecture details, the programming problem, or a solution, and its remaining content is promotional.
subtopics: Spark execution plans, memory, transformations, and actions
